agent.result_text:
All 34 tests pass and the build succeeds.

## Summary

I replaced the string `membershipTier` with a numeric `membershipLevel` (1–3) across the application:

**`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — swapped the `membershipTier` string property in the `Owner` schema for a `membershipLevel` integer (`minimum: 1`, `maximum: 3`), which regenerates `OwnerDto` with `getMembershipLevel()`/`setMembershipLevel()` at build time.

**`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — replaced the `membershipTier(owner)` mapping and method with `membershipLevel(owner)`, which computes: start at 1, +1 when an email is present, +1 when `namesakeCount` is 0, capped at 3 (level 4 reserved for tenure). This drops the old GOLD-household logic entirely, so I also removed the now-unused `ownerRepository` field, the `isGoldHousehold` helper, and their imports.

**`src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — the create audit line now records `membershipLevel` instead of the (previously implicit) tier. I build the `OwnerDto` before logging so the audit records exactly the level returned in the response, keeping a single source of truth.

The behaviour changes match the new tests: a unique owner with an email → level 3; a household member with no email and namesake 0 → level 2 (no more GOLD promotion); `membershipTier` no longer appears in responses; and the audit line contains the level.
